summary: UC Berkeley's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, run with its Center for African Studies, is a ten-year partnership funding 201 master's students from African countries, with leadership and career support alongside the degree.
covers: Full support for a Berkeley master's degree, including tuition and living costs.
Leadership development, mentoring and career support through the programme.
A cohort and alumni network across Africa.
eligibility: Citizens of African countries applying to an eligible Berkeley master's programme.
The programme recruits widely across Africa and especially encourages women, applicants with disabilities and refugees.
Demonstrated financial need and commitment to giving back.
how_to_apply: Choose an eligible Berkeley master's programme and check its departmental admission deadline.
Apply to the programme through Berkeley's graduate application and indicate your interest in the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
Many departmental deadlines fall in early December for the following autumn.
Follow the programme website for its own additional steps and information sessions.
watch_out: Your deadline is your department's, not a single programme date.
Only some Berkeley master's programmes are eligible — check the list first.
Berkeley's graduate application fee may apply; check whether the programme offers a waiver.

faq.q: Is there a separate scholarship application?
faq.a: No. You apply to an eligible master's programme, and admitted applicants can be nominated for the Scholars Program. If your programme has several admission rounds, apply in the first round — later rounds are not considered.

faq.q: Do I have to return to Africa?
faq.a: That is the aim. Scholars are expected to return home after graduating and after any optional practical training their visa allows; some go on to work in another African country in their field.

faq.q: How long will Berkeley keep recruiting?
faq.a: The programme says it will recruit Mastercard Foundation Scholars through the fall of 2028.
